title: Legacy 2.11 wheel is built from the source tree before the sdist, not from the sdist
answers: how do I build the 2.11 wheel with setup.py package_data included
build mlflow 2.11 wheel and sdist locally
why build wheel with python -m build --wheel instead of from sdist
run dev/build.py skinny or release locally
body:
Run `python dev/build.py --package-type skinny` or `--package-type release` from the repository root; it calls `python -m build --wheel` first, then `python -m build --sdist`, both through dev/build.py:build.
The wheel is built directly from the tree so setup.py package_data (UI for release; alembic and recipes data for skinny) is bundled; the sdist is built second.
The release path needs mlflow/server/js/build populated first (see dev/build.py:main guard).
Constraints: the module docstring says a sdist-to-wheel build would drop these assets, but a review comment reported the built sdist containing them; treat the sdist contents as unverified and keep the direct tree wheel build. Do not use `python -m build` with no flags as a substitute, since it does the sdist-to-wheel path.
applies: Local or CI packaging of branch-2.11 via the legacy setup.py layout.
says: Built release package is missing the user interface static assets when installed.
The lightweight package distribution fails to bundle database migration files during build.
How do I create complete distribution packages containing the web user interface locally?
Release builds are missing front end web assets after installing from packaged archives.
search: Packaging branch-2.11 with dev/build.py builds the wheel directly from the source tree before the sdist so setup.py package_data assets are included. The script runs python -m build --wheel followed by python -m build --sdist for skinny or release package types, with release requiring mlflow/server/js/build to be populated first. Bare python -m build without flags must not be used because it executes the unverified sdist-to-wheel sequence.
